source: `spark serve --help` on a release binary built from Atlas-Inf/atlas at bdcccc2c (cargo build --release -p spark-server --no-default-features --features cuda), plus the source for the six ATLAS_* environment knobs, which have no --help entry.
notes: Atlas publishes no releases or tags and every build reports the same version string, `spark 1.0.0-beta-preview`, so that string identifies nothing; the version here is the commit, as with the sparkinfer registry entry. Two things to know before reading the defaults. FIRST, several booleans are tri-state Option<bool> (gdn-fused-norm, ssm-batched-recurrent, prefill-varlen-batch, exact-verify, ssm-tail-midchunk, disable-tool-grammar, content-loop-watchdog, high-speed-swap-graph): their absence means 'the engine decides', not false, so their default is null and an explicitly passed false is NOT dropped from the fingerprint. That is the safe direction and it is deliberate. SECOND, six knobs have no flag at all and are read from the environment; they are registered here as params with the environment variable named in each help string, the same convention the sparkinfer entry uses, because the published Atlas recipes turn several of them on and a fingerprint that dropped them would merge configurations that measure differently by 20% or more. kv-cache-dtype's default is null and not fp8: precedence is flag, then the model's MODEL.toml [behavior].default_kv_dtype, then fp8, so the effective default is model-dependent. `profile` is a bare switch; the `[default: 2]` that appears in its help block belongs to a neighbouring flag with no name of its own in the long help.
